info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description:
Public VM and control-plane API contract. Backend VM endpoints expose the same wire
shapes; backend-specific feature limitations are returned as
`ErrorResponse` with `code: "unsupported_operation"`.

post.description:
Create a new VM by forking from an image, an existing VM ID, or
a VM name within an org. Exactly one of `source_image`,
`source_vm_id`, or `source_vm_name` must be set. Forking a VM
owned by another org requires that VM to be `public: true`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Narrow to a single backend region (e.g. `us-west-2`). When omitted, the response aggregates across every configured region.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Narrow to a single backend provider. `aws` returns only arkerd-managed (host-backed) VMs; `aws-burst` returns only Lambda-managed VMs. When omitted, both are returned merged.

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; include only VMs that most recently started at or after this time.

parameters.name: started_before
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; include only VMs that most recently started at or before this time.

200.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs at or after this time.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Unix epoch seconds; include runs before this time.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider filter. `aws` maps to host-backed runs; `aws-burst` maps to Lambda-backed runs.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of rows to return.

parameters.name: lite
parameters.description: When true, omit large input/output previews where supported by the backend.

200.description: Runs visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.

get.description: Control-plane listing of run activity visible to the authenticated caller across VMs, providers, and regions.

post.description:
Run a command. Foreground execution is the portable baseline.
Optional `background`, `session_id`, `network`, `signal`,
`acquire`/`release`, and per-run resource overrides may return
`unsupported_operation` on backends that don't support them.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Single executable path to launch (no shell-splitting). Defaults to the login shell.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: E2B-style persistence. When true (default), disconnecting keeps the shell running so the same session_id can RECONNECT to it (recent scrollback is replayed); when false the shell is torn down on disconnect. {"type":"kill"} or the server idle TTL destroy a persistent shell.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Browser auth: a short-lived ticket from POST .../pty-ticket, used in place of the Authorization header (which a browser WebSocket cannot set).

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying an interactive pseudo-terminal in the VM, reusing the same in-guest PTY as SSH. Auth on the upgrade is a Bearer key (a key may only attach to its own org's VMs) OR a ?ticket= for browsers. Reopening with the same session_id RECONNECTS to the same running shell when persist=true (scrollback replayed). Wire format: server→client Binary frames are raw terminal output (ANSI escapes/colors intact); client→server Binary frames are stdin bytes (control chars like 0x03=Ctrl-C raise SIGINT via the guest tty); client→server Text frames are JSON control: {"type":"resize","cols":N,"rows":M}, {"type":"kill"}, {"type":"ping"}. A plain socket close DETACHES (persist) or tears down; {"type":"kill"} always destroys. Caps: one live attachment per session, ARKER_PTY_MAX_PER_VM per VM, ARKER_PTY_MAX_PER_ORG per org (429 past limits); oversized stdin (>64KiB) or control (>4KiB) frames close the connection; idle (ARKER_PTY_IDLE_SECS) closes the connection.

101.description: Switching Protocols — the WebSocket PTY stream is established.

post.description: Returns a short-lived (5 min, multi-use) ticket for opening the PTY WebSocket from a browser, which cannot send an Authorization header. Bearer-authed; the caller must own the VM. Open wss://.../pty?ticket=<ticket> with it. The ticket is a stateless HMAC bound to (org, vm, session), so it validates on any node.

Create a persistent sync: ensure a Filesystem exists (creating
one if requested) and bind-mount it into this VM at `path`.
Bidirectional by virtue of being a mount — there is no separate
sync-direction parameter. Returns `ErrorResponse` code
`conflict` if a sync already exists at `path`.

200.description: Read or write result, matching the request op.

post.description:
Read or write files in the VM filesystem. Op-discriminated:
`{op:"read",path}` reads a file (inline content for small files, a
presigned GET URL for large ones); `{op:"write",writes:[...]}` writes,
each entry an inline chunk or a presigned-upload step. Binding a
filesystem into the VM is the separate `/v1/vms/{id}/syncs` resource.

200.description: Created tunnel. `auth_token` is returned only once for authenticated tunnels.
Delete result. The filesystem must not be mounted by any VM (no remaining `Sync` referencing it).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous page's `next_cursor`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Max items per page. Backend caps may apply.

TunnelKey.name: key
TunnelKey.description: Recoverable tunnel identity returned as `Tunnel.tunnel_key` and embedded in tunnel URLs.

UnsupportedOperation.description: The request is valid, but this backend does not support the requested operation or option.

value.message: background runs are not supported on this backend

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. `unsupported_operation` means the backend doesn't implement the requested optional feature.

VmState.description: Unified lifecycle state for a VM or a Session. `idle` means no command is currently executing; `running` means a command is in flight.

RunState.description:
Lifecycle state for a Run. `running` = command in flight.
`completed` = the command ran to completion; `exit_code` conveys
success (0) or a non-zero program exit (a non-zero exit is still
`completed`). `failed` = the platform could not run or finish the
command (host died, evicted mid-run, exec error); `fail_reason`
explains why, distinct from the program's `stderr`. `cancelled` =
cancelled by the client.

TunnelState.description:
`starting` = backend is allocating the tunnel; `open` = accepting
connections; `closed` = torn down or never came up.

source_vm_id.description: Global VM identifier. Org is inferred from the row.

source_vm_name.description: VM name within an org. Defaults `source_org_id` to the caller's org. A different org must be either the Arker org (for the public goldens `arkuntu` / `ubuntu`) or one with a `public: true` VM by that name.

source_org_id.description: Optional explicit org context for `source_vm_name`. SDK auto-fills the Arker org when forking the public goldens.

name.description: Optional name for the new VM, scoped to the caller's org.

public.description: Make the new VM publicly forkable from other orgs.

tunnel.description: Optional VM-scoped tunnel customization. Omitting it allocates an open any-port tunnel where supported.

env.description: Optional environment-variable overrides for this session.

public.description: When `true`, other orgs can fork this VM (but cannot run on it).

root_source_vm_id.description: ID of the root (deepest-ancestor) source VM, if this VM was created by a chain of forks. None for VMs forked directly from an image.

root_source_vm_name.description: Name of the root source VM. Populated together with `root_source_vm_id`.

max_vcpus.description: Hard vCPU ceiling for a fork of this VM (KVM slot count). Requesting more fails the run.

max_memory_mib.description: Hard memory ceiling (MiB) a fork can hotplug up to.

worker_id.description: Worker host that owns this VM. Used by routers to populate caches without a fresh PlanetScale lookup.

acquire.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to ensure are
pre-allocated (warm) before the run starts. Values: `cpu`,
`memory`, `disk`. Example: `"cpu,memory"`.

release.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to release after the run
finishes. Values: `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`. `"cpu"` frees
vCPU but keeps memory hot for the next run on this VM;
`"cpu,memory,disk"` is a full release (closest to a
suspend).

run_id.description: The run's own id. Present for executed runs; absent for operation acks (release/signal) with no run record.

state.description: Lifecycle state — "completed" for this shape. Read this (not the variant) for completion, uniformly with the run-status (`Run`) shape.

stdout_encoding.description:
TODO(encoding-normalize): goal is to always emit utf-8 from
every source so this field becomes unnecessary. Until then
the SDK uses it to decode.

memory_requested_mib.description: ARK-107: requested total memory (MiB) when this run carried an explicit memory override. Absent when the run had no memory override.

memory_achieved_mib.description: ARK-107: achieved total memory (MiB) after the run's resize. Memory shrink is best-effort, so this can exceed memory_requested_mib when guest pages are pinned. Absent when the run had no memory override.

memory_partial.description: ARK-107: true when the run's memory shrink was partial (achieved differs from requested beyond the virtio-mem block granularity). The command still ran at the achieved footprint (best-effort); this flags the gap instead of a silent success. Defaults false.

state.description: Lifecycle state — "running" for a backgrounded run.

fail_reason.description: System failure explanation when `state` is `failed` (e.g. "host died: <id>", "evicted mid-run"). Distinct from `stderr`, which is the program's own error output. Null for runs that ran to completion.
System failure explanation when `state` is `failed` — see `Run.fail_reason`. Distinct from the program's `stderr`.

vm_id.description: The VM this tunnel belongs to. Always populated so flat tunnel listings work without restructuring.

run_id.description: The Run that opened this tunnel, if any. VM-scoped tunnels created at fork time or via `POST /vms/{id}/tunnels` have `run_id: null`.

tunnel_key.description: Recoverable tunnel identity embedded in URLs (`p{port}-{key}`). Not a secret. Present on VM-scoped tunnel responses.

auth_token.description: One-time bearer secret returned only when allocating an authenticated tunnel; never echoed on listings.

memory_requested_mib.description: Requested total memory (MiB), present only when the request carried memory_mib.

memory_achieved_mib.description: Achieved total memory (MiB). virtio-mem unplug is best-effort, so this can exceed memory_requested_mib when guest pages are pinned.

memory_partial.description: True when a memory target was requested but the runtime could not reach it (achieved differs from requested beyond virtio-mem block granularity). Treat as target-not-met.

path.description: VM-side path where the filesystem is mounted. Same field name as used by `SyncReadRequest.path`.

ports.description: Allowed VM ports for this tunnel. Omitted, null, or empty means any port.

auth_mode.description: `open` allows unauthenticated tunnel requests. `authenticated` returns a one-time bearer `auth_token` and requires it on tunnel requests.
